entities.name: Haemorhous mexicanus
observations: House finch; formerly Carpodacus mexicanus. The direct study examined song and bill traits across a continuous urbanization gradient.

entities.name: PMID:25426158
observations: Badyaev et al. 2014, Frontiers in Zoology: Song characteristics track bill morphology along a gradient of urbanization in house finches.

Urbanization was summarized from seven land-use variables plus human population density; urban birds had longer, narrower bills and higher minimum song frequencies, while upper song-frequency limits declined with bill morphology.
The retrieved evidence does not establish a repertoire comparison or provide complete statistical coefficients.

entities.name: PMID:18507745
observations: Badyaev et al. 2008, Evolution: Evolution on a local scale: developmental, functional, and genetic bases of divergence in bill form and associated changes in song structure between adjacent habitats.
Urban and Sonoran desert house finches differed in food-resource selection, bill morphology, bite force, and courtship song; urban birds had larger bills.
The retrieved abstract does not specify song acoustic variables, repertoire metrics, or exact song-bill statistical tests.

entities.name: Urban bill-song tracking
observations: In house finches, urbanization-associated bill divergence tracks song-frequency divergence: longer bills are associated with lower upper frequency limits, while urban noise is associated with higher minimum frequency.
Evidence supports coordinated bill and song-acoustic change across urbanization, but not a demonstrated repertoire-bill relationship.

entities.name: GHB
observations: Acute recreational intoxication can cause profound somnolence or coma, respiratory depression, bradycardia, hypotension, and hypothermia.
At intoxicating concentrations, GHB produces CNS depression through GABA-B receptor activation in addition to GHB-specific receptor activity.

entities.name: Opioids
observations: Opioid overdose classically causes miosis, respiratory depression, bradycardia, and stupor or coma through mu-opioid receptor activation.
Pinpoint pupils make opioid toxicity an important competing diagnosis in this presentation.

entities.name: GHB toxidrome
observations: Rave-associated profound CNS and respiratory depression with hypothermia, hypotension, and bradycardia is most consistent with GHB intoxication; miosis remains a competing opioid clue.
